# GNU tar mtime Handling

Measured on GNU tar 1.35 (Debian slim container filesystem). Facts relevant to
designing mtime-based delta transfers: what timestamp precision an archive
round-trips, and which timestamp a date filter actually tests.

## Default create format stores whole-second mtimes

The default archive format (GNU tar 1.35's default, not `--format=posix`)
stores modification times as whole seconds. Fractional seconds are not
preserved.

Verified: a source file with mtime `2026-11-20 14:56:45.529257774`, archived
with a default `tar cf` and extracted, came back with mtime
`2026-11-20 14:56:45.000000000`.

Consequence: comparing an extracted file against a host file that carries a
nanosecond mtime with a sub-second test reports the difference. Bash's
`[[ file1 -nt file2 ]]` on a host file in the same second but with nonzero
nanoseconds evaluated as the host file being newer. Comparing whole seconds
(`stat -c %Y`, or truncating nanoseconds before comparison) removes the false
positive.

## `--newer` tests mtime **or** ctime

`--newer=DATE` (long form `--after-date=DATE`) selects an entry when its
**mtime or its ctime** is newer than DATE. `--newer-mtime=DATE` restricts the
test to mtime alone.

Verified: a file with mtime `2020-01-01` and ctime `2026-11-20` was included by
`tar cf out.tar --newer=2021-01-01`. The same file was excluded by
`--newer-mtime=2021-01-01`.

A file whose data predates the stamp can therefore appear in a `--newer`
selection purely because its metadata changed later (touch, chmod, chown, rename,
or a rewrite of its ctime by an earlier extraction).

## Filtering vs traversal

`--newer` / `--after-date` has no effect on which directories are traversed.
It filters the entries written to the archive; directory walking is unchanged.

## Consequences for mtime-based delta transfers

- Extracting an archive writes new files, so their ctime becomes the extraction
  time regardless of the archived mtime. The default GNU archive format does
  not store ctime, so extraction cannot restore it. A later
  `tar --newer=<stamp>` on the extracted tree can therefore include files whose
  data mtime predates `<stamp>`. Correctness is unaffected; the cost is
  transferred bytes.
- `--newer-mtime` avoids that inflation when only data changes are wanted, at
  the cost of missing metadata-only changes (a file whose contents are unchanged
  but whose owner, mode, or link count changed will not be selected).
- Combined with whole-second archive mtimes, a delta stamp should be compared
  at whole-second granularity. Sub-second stamps either over-select (files in
  the boundary second) or, when the extracted side is truncated to `.000`,
  mis-order files within that second.
